purpose: How Python finds out which kind of worker an item needs, once, from data. Order: the item's own `role` (set by a lead or the planner) wins; else the item's `kind` through this table; else the item goes to the planner to be labelled. The model never decides its own role and never invents one; a planner's label is a work-list change a lead reads.
person_work_why: a decision is the owner's, hardware is physical, deletes and consolidations are cautious human calls (a worker may investigate or propose, never do them)
needs_label: every other kind (research and review too: the researcher has no tool yet and the reviewer is a system role, so neither can take an item by kind), a missing kind and an unknown kind: measure, carried-from-ledger, tracking, trial, follow-up, platform... The word does not say what the hand-back is, so the planner proposes a role as a work-list change.
evidence: open agent items on 2026-10-22: enable 174, feature 96, carried-from-ledger 74, fix 64, build 32, measure 31, none 17, standard 8, decision 6, adopt 5, consolidate 4, hardware 3, delete 3, replace 2, test 2, others 1 each; roles named on items: investigator 23, builder 15, email-watcher 9 (Book Factory's own), researcher 5
